source.author: verg
source.text: Accipe nunc Danaum insidias, et crimine ab uno disce omnes.
source.text_original: Accipe nunc Danaum insidias, et crimine ab uno / disce omnes.
source.text_english: Now hear the treachery of the Greeks, and from one crime learn all.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Sed ut infinita praeteream et ostendam tibi, uir omnium nobilium Christianissime, Christianorum nobilissime, cuius modi falsitates in epistulae translatione reprehendant, ipsius epistulae ponam cum Graeco sermone principium, ut ex uno crimine intellegantur et cetera: , , , quod ego ita uertisse me memini: oportebat nos, dilectissime, clericatus honore non abuti in superbiam.
reuse.text_original: Sed ut infinita praeteream et ostendam tibi, uir omnium nobilium Christianissime, Christianorum nobilissime, cuius modi falsitates in epistulae translatione reprehendant, ipsius epistulae ponam cum Graeco sermone principium, ut ex uno crimine intellegantur et cetera: ἔδει ἡμᾶς, ἀγαπητέ, μὴ τῇ οἰήσει τῶν κλήρων φέρεσθαι, quod ego ita uertisse me memini: oportebat nos, dilectissime, clericatus honore non abuti in superbiam.
reuse.text_english: But to pass over innumerable things, and to show you, man most Christian of all the noble, and most noble of the Christians, what kind of falsehoods they criticize in the translation of the letter, I shall set down the beginning of the letter itself together with the Greek text, so that from one fault the rest may be understood: , , , which I remember having translated thus: it was fitting that we, dearest one, should not abuse the honor of the clergy to our own pride.
